function: Joint AP power control and precoding (transmission matrix F) for cell-free massive MIMO, maximizing sum spectral efficiency with a sparse multi-dimensional GNN (p. 2-4).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO: 9 APs x 8 antennas and 8 single-antenna UEs (power control); 4 UEs and 16 antennas (precoding); no RIS; band not stated (p. 4).
method: Sparse multi-dimensional GNN (SP-MDGNN) with learnable adjacency and threshold pruning, 5 GNN layers of 256 units, trained end-to-end on an SE-maximization loss, no labels (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated Rayleigh fading with path loss -30.5 - 36.7 log10(d) (power control); SV model, 4 clusters, 5 rays (precoding); 10,000 training, 2,000 testing samples (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained and tested on the same simulated setting (10,000 train, 2,000 test samples); only the pruning threshold varies; no unseen scenario reported (p. 4).
baselines: WMMSE (classical), original MDGNN and attention-based MDGNN (A-MDGNN) as learned GNN baselines (p. 5).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency (mean and CDF), computation time, sparsity and performance retention, harmonic mean score of both (p. 4-5).
complexity: Measured computation time for equal samples and hardware; SP-MDGNN cuts complexity 48% versus MDGNN in the joint task, 55% and 49% in the separate tasks (p. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 4: "Rayleigh fading channels, modeled by the SV model" (the authors' own simulator with Rayleigh fading, an SV model and a path-loss formula; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is named).
q2_support: p. 4: "Datasets include 10,000 training and 2,000 testing samples" (a split of the same simulated setting; the conclusion on p. 5 claims robustness across network conditions, but no test with another number of APs, UEs, antennas or scenario is reported).
q3_support: p. 5: "the baseline MDGNN, the attention-based MDGNN (A-MDGNN), and the WMMSE algorithm" (WMMSE is the non-learned baseline; MDGNN is the earlier published learned method [12], p. 1; all are compared on SE in Fig. 4).
q4_support: p. 5: "based on measuring the computation time required to process" (identical samples and hardware for each method; "48% reduction in computational complexity" versus MDGNN).
q5_support: p. 4: "Datasets include 10,000 training and 2,000 testing samples" (the authors' own simulated data; no code or data link and no public dataset anywhere in the paper).
notes: Read all 5 pages and pages 4-5 as images (Figs. 3-5). Included: correspondence that proposes and evaluates a learned method for power control and precoding in cell-free massive MIMO; physical layer; simulation results; APs have several antennas. Area 3: the network output is the transmission matrix F, whose norm sets power and whose direction sets the beam (p. 2-3). q1 is 0 because the channel is the authors' own Rayleigh/SV simulator with a path-loss formula and no standardized or measured source (p. 4). q2 is 0: only one train/test split per task is reported; the sentence on p. 5 about robustness 'validated across a myriad of network conditions' is not backed by any reported experiment. q3 is borderline: WMMSE is the classical baseline and MDGNN [12] is a published learned method ('the original MDGNN method', p. 1), but SP-MDGNN extends MDGNN, so the reviewer may read it as an ablation, in which case q3 would be 0; A-MDGNN is an attention variant and is not counted. q4 rests on measured computation time (p. 5, Fig. 5b). PDF is arXiv v1 (2 Jul 2025) of 'Joint Power Control and Precoding for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Sparse Multi-Dimensional Graph Neural Networks'; the DOI-title match could not be checked with the allowed files.
